newsitem.title: INDIA: Rupee gains against dollar in Indian forex market.
newsitem.headline: Rupee gains against dollar in Indian forex market.

text.p: The Indian rupee has risen sharply on the forward dollar market and is firm in spot trading after the central bank's move to boost liquidity and trigger interest rate cuts, bankers said on Wednesday.
The rupee was quoted at 35.59/60 to the dollar in midsession trade on Wednesday.

Dollars for April delivery were quoted at 1.27/1.30 rupees over the spot rate on Wednesday, compared with 1.30/1.34 rupees on Tuesday, the first day of trading after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) released its monetary policy on Saturday.
April dollar was quoted at a premium of 1.57/1.60 rupees at the close of trading on Friday, dealers said.
This implied a revision of April dollar to 36.90 rupees on Wednesday, from 37.17 on Friday.
RBI governor Chakravarty Rangarajan told Reuters Financial Television on Monday he expected the rupee to be stable against the dollar at current levels as demand and supply are balanced.
Bank dealers and company treasurers said they were not sure that the rupee had peaked in the forward dollar market.
"I feel this (annualised premia of 7.5 percent for six months) is the right level, on fundamentals," said Ranjit Shah, director of Su-Raj Diamonds, one of India's leading diamond export firms.
Shah said corporates could borrow in the overseas markets at around the same interest rate based on LIBOR.
Some other market participants said the rupee had not peaked against the dollar.

"I think 120 paise (1.20 rupees for April dollars) is the next level the market will aim," said Yeshwant Rao, deputy general manager of Pinnacle Finance Ltd, an associate of textile firm Arvind Mills.
RBI cut the cash reserve ratio (CRR) for banks to release more than 85 billion rupees into the system. The CRR cut will be carried out in four stages.
"When call money rates are coming down, no one wants to convert dollars into rupees," said a dealer. Banks swap their dollar funds to lend in rupees.
With six-month forward premia at around eight percent, the swap cost works out to about 14 percent, inclusive of about six percent interest payable on their dollar deposits.

The first CRR cut is expected to release about 20 billion rupees into the banking system in the next fortnight, pushing down overnight call rates to between six and eight percent from 8.5 to 9.0 percent on Wednesday.
The rupee has been gaining in the spot market against the dollar in recent months after a surge in dollar supplies from foreign direct investment and overseas equity raised by Indian firms.
The RBI has been continuously buying dollars in recent months to arrest the rupee's rise against the dollar.
